title: The Young Indiana Jones
subtitle: A small squad, revving engines, and a gloomy cave make for a story that never goes out of fashion.

items.speaker: Kanjira
items.text: Woo-hoo! Alright, sit tight!

items.speaker: Kanjira
items.text: Let's GO!!

items.speaker: Matilda
items.text: Waaaaah?!

items.speaker: Villager 1
items.text: *coughs* You little j**k again! D**n it, Sinha, for one last time, don't borrow that annoying human thing to her!
The bright-yellow tuk tuk drifts in a beautiful arc on the soft road, the brown sand kicked up in the air covering up the curses of the passer-by.

items.speaker: Matilda
items.text: Slow down, slow down! We are going too fast!

items.speaker: Matilda
items.text: Waaaah! Is this thing really under control?!

items.speaker: Kanjira
items.text: Hey!
As the tuk tuk roars along, the marigold petals are flying wildly in the wind.

items.speaker: Kanjira
items.text: Not yet best part! Hold that bar tight!

items.speaker: Matilda
items.text: Waaah ...
Street

items.speaker: Matilda
items.text: Whuu ... phew ...

items.speaker: Kanjira
items.text: Woo-hoo! How you feel, my guest?

items.speaker: Matilda
items.text: *vomits*

items.speaker: Kanjira
items.text: Oh, I'm sorry. You must not be used to this. Here, use it.
As Kanjira passes over the hem of her skirt, Matilda takes out a handkerchief from her pocket in silence.

items.speaker: Kanjira
items.text: If you want your silk dirty. Fine, you look very decent after all.

items.speaker: Kanjira
items.text: And, here it is.
The shrine is apparently an old one, judging by the worn bricks. The smell of sticky spices in the air is almost suffocating.

items.speaker: Matilda
items.text: What's this smell? Is it ... *coughs*

items.speaker: Kanjira
items.text: Smell of full white musk and sanders, calming palo santo and cinnamon. Hah! You feel your chakra open?

items.speaker: Kanjira
items.text: But, I can also smell, hmm, a lot of mango. That smells good.
Kanjira glances at the stone wall to measure its height and then nods.

items.speaker: Kanjira
items.text: Okay. Jump over this wall, and we are in!

items.speaker: Matilda
items.text: Jump over it?! I thought there is at least a hidden side door!

items.speaker: Kanjira
items.text: To see the closed cave, you must pay a price!

items.speaker: Matilda
items.text: Ah. So this is your "local connections"!

items.speaker: Kanjira
items.text: Um. Well, that mean tuk tuk, my guest! No tuk tuk this village is faster than that! Uncle Sinha is not so nice and lend me if I don't give him my lunch money!

items.speaker: Kanjira
items.text: My route don't need entrance ticket! Shouldn't you give me credit?
Even if she is busted, Kanjira is not embarrassed at all. On the contrary, she looks a bit proud. She puts her hands together to form a temporary "stepping stone."

items.speaker: Kanjira
items.text: Now come! Although I think you don't like this "rude" behavi- ...

items.speaker: Matilda
items.text: Humph!
Ignoring the "stepping stone," Matilda raises her arms and jumps up the wall deftly.

items.speaker: Kanjira
items.text: Hmm?

items.speaker: Matilda
items.text: I was thoughtful and considerate enough not to wipe my nose on your skirt, yet you repay my kindness with contempt. Climbing over a wall of this height is really a piece of cake!

items.speaker: Matilda
items.text: So? Do you need a hand getting up here?
Matilda looks down proudly from the top of the wall.

items.speaker: Kanjira
items.text: Huh! Weirdo.
Mor Pankh Shrine
The shrine is shrouded in thick smoke and packed with pious believers, resembling a legged cloud with the smell of spices.
The two small figures sneak into the shadow in the corner while avoiding the believers in their way.

items.speaker: Matilda
items.text: I don't know what this skulking was for! You'd better not be lying!

items.speaker: Kanjira
items.text: Nom nom.

items.speaker: Matilda
items.text: Hey, what's that in your hand?!

items.speaker: Kanjira
items.text: You want a bite? The prayers are so pious, so don't worry, the fruits is tasty! Nom nom, like I expect, so sweet.

items.speaker: Matilda
items.text: When did you ... Did you take it from the offerings?!

items.speaker: Kanjira
items.text: Don't mind! Manka, come back.
A little black snake creeps up her arm quietly.

items.speaker: Kanjira
items.text: By the way, I hope you is not afraid of snakes. I'm a special kind.

items.speaker: Matilda
items.text: And I'm curious about what exactly you are referring to. Specially rude, or specially annoying?

items.speaker: Kanjira
items.text: Why so angr- ... I mean, um, I'm arcanist. Hope I don't scare you. Relax, I'm not like others.

items.speaker: Matilda
items.text: Are you serious? Can't you tell I'm also an excellent, one of the best, arcanist?
Matilda jumps up with a jerk out of excitement, but then she notices the crowds and has to crouch down again very quickly.

items.speaker: Matilda
items.text: So you were lying to me! Spoke about all those good virtues you can see in me.

items.speaker: Kanjira
items.text: Hey! It's not my fault! You doesn't look like one!
Kanjira drops the mango core and scans Matilda in slight surprise.

items.speaker: Kanjira
items.text: I thought all arcanists except me are like ...

items.speaker: Matilda
items.text: Like what?

items.speaker: Kanjira
items.text: Like the villagers, those old mans, yell when they see humans, like annoying monkeys or crowing chickens. They even drive humans away, don't care they is here to help.

items.speaker: Kanjira
items.text: Why you think only the train station is tidy and clean? Humans in other places is all drive away!

items.speaker: Kanjira
items.text: I'm not like them because ... Anyways, I never thought there is more arcanist like me.
Kanjira speaks in a quiet voice. A confused look appears on her face.

items.speaker: Matilda
items.text: Humph, if you ask me, I'd say you read too little and know too little.

items.speaker: Matilda
items.text: I suggest you follow my example and adopt the style of a real arcanist.

items.speaker: Kanjira
items.text: Fine, fine! Oh, Manka say there is just a few people outside, so up your head, stay confident, and walk out like we paid!

items.speaker: Matilda
items.text: Have you been listening or not?!
North Cave
Following Kanjira, Matilda goes through the smoke and arrives at the entrance to the cave.

items.speaker: Kanjira
items.text: Ha! Nice. Nobody around as usual!

items.speaker: Kanjira
items.text: But I still suggest you be careful, since ... Hmm, I understand the damage when digging. Just don't involve me if you must break something!
Matilda looks up, not hearing a word of her mutter.

items.speaker: Matilda
items.text: So this is "the Head of Vindre"?
The top of the cave looks like a black hole. No one knows where it will lead or what it will devour.

items.speaker: Kanjira
items.text: Tsk tsk, dark and scary. But this is what must go through on the way to treasure, just like you must say "Open Sesame," right?

items.speaker: Matilda
items.text: I really don't know what to make of this "treasure" you've been mumbling about. I hope you didn't get the wrong idea.

items.speaker: Kanjira
items.text: Ah. I see what you mean here. Relax. I will zip my lips and tell no one.
She zips her mouth shut and nods sincerely.

items.speaker: Kanjira
items.text: I'll just stay here, then. Everything good luck!

items.speaker: Matilda
items.text: Ah? Anyway, despite all the strange things you've been talking about along the way, you have successfully taken me here as promised. I guess here is where we part! Thank you.
After bidding her goodbye, Matilda turns around to walk toward the cave while browsing the documents in her hand.
Soon she is devoured by the bottomless darkness.

items.speaker: Kanjira
items.text: Sincerest wishes to you, my brave guest! Whether a giant snake or dragon, as long as you find the legendary treasure, we'll meet again! Hee hee.
Footsteps echo inside the cave like a piece of poorly composed percussion music.

items.speaker: Matilda
items.text: This mural seems to be related to that myth! Here, on this paper! Let me see.
There is a huge mural carved on the wall, spreading to the end of her sight.
She turns the pages of the notebook quickly.

items.speaker: Matilda
items.text: Found it! "Before the Serpent struck in night sky, the stone house of Asura rose to the north of the Head of Vindre."

items.speaker: Matilda
items.text: "The master of the stone has acted, with countless feet, with countless eyes, to trip, to pry, in bringing the blessed house of men to rest."

items.speaker: Matilda
items.text: Wow, impressive! Perhaps this is the origin of some arcane creature.

items.speaker: Matilda
items.text: "The Serpent struck," that is to say, the best time to practice on the celestial energy is when the comet goes across the sky?

items.speaker: Matilda
items.text: "Long darkness reaches the men as the Serpent's tail reveals itself. Some are sent down the great slopes and never return ..."

items.speaker: Matilda
items.text: "... for desire is the infallible devourer. "

items.speaker: Matilda
items.text: Desire, hmm, I should meditate before practice.

items.speaker: Matilda
items.text: "The circle of everything ends at the tip of the great tail, all ..."
THUD!
The echo has disappeared.
Behind her, there is nothing but boundless darkness.

items.speaker: Matilda
items.text: Did I hear it wrong?

items.speaker: Matilda
items.text: No ...

items.speaker: Matilda
items.text: Come into the light! Who, who is there?
Her voice ripples out. Its echoes and the echoes of the echoes reverberate between the walls of the cave.
There is no response.

items.speaker: Matilda
items.text: This doesn't seem right.

items.speaker: Matilda
items.text: Was this statue posing like this earlier?
While Matilda is still wondering, the statues in her sights start to move.

items.speaker: Matilda
items.text: Aah!
The benevolent-looking statues, which were sitting in lotus position, are now struggling in a twisted way to break free from the wall.

items.speaker: Matilda
items.text: Not good! Time to retreat.
She turns around immediately and runs toward the exit, yet the ground is pulling her back like a rolling carpet.

items.speaker: Matilda
items.text: What?! Aah!
She can feel her chin hitting hard against the rock.
One arm, two, three, and more of them are growing out from both sides of the statues, each with a glossy eyeball embedded within.

items.speaker: Matilda
items.text: What? What is this!
Following the slight noise, every eye turns to the girl lying on the ground.

items.speaker: Matilda
items.text: Oh! Hurry up. Get yourself together! Think what you have learned and practiced in the past!
